It's been full of security problems for a long time and isn't really necessary anymore. With HTML5 you can play videos without flash. Youtube has had that capability for most of its videos for quite a while.

Flash is basically a method of playing back media or software within a browser / runtime system (little like Java), for YouTube it was the playback software that just enabled viewing of the videos being streamed from YouTubes data centers and a lot of other sites used it in the same way. Think of it like an embedded version of a media player like VLC, Media Center Classic or Windows Media Player.

Everyone is ditching it because of the massive amount of security flaws being discovered, some of which completely compromises a computer / browser leaving it open to run whatever the attacker wants. Google has been pushing HTLM5 as a replacement for Flash and have even changed over to a default HTML5 player on YouTube, chances are you have been using Flashes replacement for the last 8 months or so so without noticing it, HTML5 is efficient enough that web developers don't need to rely on things like Flash or Java to create interactive and Adobe has been winding down support for a long time now and even releasing tools to convert flash to HTML5

Also HTML5 is a format that was designed by the Internet community while Flash was made only by Adobe, way back when. If you have a smartphone instead of a traditional cellphone it should be clear to you why some old technologies just got to go.
